intro: Alaska runs its elections statewide through the Division of Elections, which has regional offices around the state.

id_rule.text: Be ready to show one form of ID, such as a voter registration card, an Alaska driver's license or state ID, a current photo ID, a military ID, or a recent utility bill, paycheck or bank statement with your name and address. If you have no ID and no election official knows you, you vote a questioned ballot.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state and local offices, plus any statewide or local measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: The deadline is the 30th day before the election, and it always falls on a Sunday.

src.label: Alaska Division of Elections — 2026 election calendar

dates.label: Early voting and in-person absentee voting
dates.detail: Anyone can vote early or absentee in person. The Division also lists extra weekend hours at its regional offices on Oct. 24, Oct. 25, Oct. 31 and Nov. 1.

src.label: Alaska Division of Elections — 2026 election calendar
Alaska Division of Elections — absentee and early voting

dates.label: Mail absentee application must be received
dates.detail: Alaska lets any voter vote absentee by mail. Applications sent by electronic transmission are due by 5 pm Alaska time on Nov. 2.

src.label: Alaska Division of Elections — 2026 election calendar
Alaska Division of Elections — absentee and early voting

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 7 am to 8 pm. A mailed ballot must be postmarked on or before Election Day.

src.label: Alaska Division of Elections — 2026 election calendar

dates.label: Last day for mailed ballots to arrive
dates.detail: Ballots mailed from inside the U.S. must be postmarked by Nov. 3 and received by this date. Ballots mailed from overseas have until Nov. 18.
